verses.text: "Here is my servant, whom I support, my chosen one, in whom I delight. I have put my Spirit on him, and he will bring justice to the nations.
He will not shout or raise his voice. He will not make his voice heard in the streets.
He will not break a bent reed, and he will not put out a flickering lamp. He will faithfully bring justice.
He will not grow weak or lose heart until he has set up justice on the earth. The islands will wait hopefully for his teaching."

This is what God the LORD says, the one who created the heavens and stretched them out, who spread out the earth and everything that grows on it, who gives breath to its people and life to those who walk on it:
"I, the LORD, have called you to do what is right. I will take hold of your hand and keep you safe. I will make you a covenant for the people and a light for the nations,
to open the eyes of the blind, to set prisoners free from the dungeon, and to bring those who sit in darkness out of the prison.
I am the LORD. That is my name. I will not give my glory to anyone else, or my praise to carved idols.
Look, the things I said before have happened, and now I tell you about new things. I tell you about them before they begin to happen."
Sing a new song to the LORD! Sing his praise from the ends of the earth, you who sail on the sea and everything in it, you islands and all who live on them.
Let the wilderness and its towns raise their voices, the villages where the people of Kedar live. Let the people of Sela sing for joy. Let them shout from the tops of the mountains!
Let them give glory to the LORD and announce his praise in the islands.
The LORD will march out like a mighty warrior. He will stir up his anger like a soldier. He will shout a battle cry. Yes, he will shout out loud, and he will defeat his enemies.
"I have kept quiet for a long time. I have been silent and held myself back. But now, like a woman giving birth, I will cry out. I will gasp and pant.
I will flatten the mountains and hills and dry up all their plants. I will turn rivers into dry land and dry up the pools.

I will lead the blind along a road they do not know. I will guide them on paths they have never known. I will turn the darkness in front of them into light and make the rough places smooth. These are the things I will do. I will not leave them.
But those who trust in idols, who say to metal images, 'You are our gods,' will be turned back in shame."
"Listen, you who are deaf! Look, you who are blind, so that you can see!
Who is blind like my servant, or deaf like the messenger I send? Who is blind like the one I made peace with, blind like the servant of the LORD?
You see many things, but you do not pay attention. Your ears are open, but you do not listen."
Because the LORD is righteous, he was pleased to make his teaching great and glorious.

But these people have been robbed and looted. All of them are trapped in pits and hidden away in prisons. They have become victims with no one to rescue them, stolen goods with no one to say, "Give them back!"
Which of you will listen to this? Who will pay close attention from now on?
Who handed Jacob over to be looted, and Israel to robbers? Was it not the LORD, against whom we have sinned? For they would not follow his ways or obey his teaching.
So he poured out his burning anger on them, and the violence of war. It surrounded them with flames, yet they did not understand. It burned them, but they did not take it to heart.
